page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5e.2xlarge is an x86_64 storage- and memory-focused virtual machine configured on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6763P-C processor clocked at 2.9 GHz, the instance delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a generous memory-to-vCPU allocation of 8.0 GB per core. The architecture does not include dedicated graphics processing units.

Integrated directly into the instance is 3839 GB of local SSD storage, providing high-capacity direct-attached non-volatile drive space without relying solely on network-attached volumes. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth rate of 20 Gbps, facilitating high-throughput node interconnectivity and steady ingress or egress across clustered deployments.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bundling of 3839 GB of local SSD capacity alongside an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio allows organizations to avoid external block storage attachments for intensive scratch space or working data sets. Because local storage is directly bound to the hardware host, durability considerations require operational planning for data replication across nodes.

The ecs.i5e.2xlarge instance is suited for storage-intensive and in-memory transactional workloads. Primary deployment targets include intermediate-scale relational databases, NoSQL engines, distributed search nodes, real-time analytics, and caching layers requiring substantial disk caching and high memory capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5e.2xlarge is an x86_64 instance built on the KVM hypervisor within the Local SSDs instance family. It is equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6763P-C processor running at 2.9 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory for an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A key attribute of the hardware configuration is the integration of 3839 GB of local SSD storage, eliminating the need for separate network-attached volumes for hot storage paths. The instance provides 20 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without attached GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With high local disk density and substantial RAM allocation relative to compute cores, the server represents an efficient deployment platform for data-heavy operations. It is matched to database servers, indexing clusters, NoSQL datastores, distributed data caching, and operational analytics workloads.
